lines.text: How far would you zoom into your fingertip to see one atom?
Ten times closer, and the ridges of your fingerprint become hills.
A thousand times, and you hit your skin cells.
Ten thousand, and one cell's nucleus fills the screen.
A million times, and there's your DNA, coiled and twisting.
At a hundred million times closer,
you finally reach a single atom.
And your fingertip holds more atoms than there are stars in our galaxy.
